history.title: A passion that became a workshop.
history.p1: Created in April 2024 by Eric Lapierre, initially as a hobby, L’atelier BREDDY Inc. grew around a passion for creating and making.
history.p2: In July 2025, the activity officially became a business. Today, Eric Lapierre and Annie Paré, co-owners, continue to develop the workshop in Granby with a focus on custom work and versatility.
history.p3: 3D design and printing, welding and metalwork, woodworking and epoxy can be brought together within the same project to keep a coherent view of the need through to the final realization.

material.title: Wood can stay natural. Epoxy can become the design.
material.p1: Epoxy does not need to be present in every project. Wood can also be worked on its own to highlight its natural appearance and create pieces that are both practical and decorative.
material.p2: When used, resin can be clear, coloured, opaque or translucent. It can fill sections of the wood, create contrast or become the main design element.
material.p3: Depending on the project, wood and epoxy can also be combined with metal or 3D-printed components when the realization requires it.

printing.title: Useful parts, not just tests.
printing.p1: 3D printing can be used for functional parts, supports, adapters, enclosures, accessories, replacement parts, custom creations and small production runs.
printing.p2: We work with PLA, PETG, ASA and Nylon (carbon fibre). Material choice depends on the part’s use, environment and desired characteristics.
